title: China's open AI models now trail the US frontier by just seven months
key_facts: Epoch AI's Capabilities Index (39 benchmarks) shows Chinese models trailing the US frontier by an average of seven months since 2023, in a range of four to fourteen months.
Every model at the absolute frontier since 2023 came from the US; no Chinese model has yet matched OpenAI's o3 (April 2025).
The first Chinese model to beat GPT-4 did so in May 2024, fourteen months after GPT-4.
Epoch found the US-China gap closely tracks the gap between closed and open-weight models: leading Chinese models (DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, GLM) are mostly open, US frontier ones mostly closed.
A Mozilla-backed analysis put the gap at about 4.4 months, with Chinese open models up to five times cheaper per task.
The Financial Times reported Tencent signed a roughly $7 billion five-year lease for 100,000 AI chips via Oracle's Southeast Asia data centres.
The article questions whether US export controls still make sense given the shrinking lead.
quote_evidence: Chinese models have trailed the US frontier by an average of seven months since 2023, with the gap ranging from as little as four months to as much as fourteen.
No Chinese model has yet matched OpenAI's o3, released in April 2025.
Epoch found the US-China gap tracks almost exactly onto the gap between closed and open-weight models generally.
why_it_matters_hint: A shrinking gap raises doubts about whether chip export controls can preserve a US lead.
event_date: Epoch AI analysis, date not stated; article 14 Oct 2026
notes: Startup Fortune article mixes Epoch AI with older Stanford AI Index data, a Mozilla-backed study and Bloomberg Intelligence figures; the opinion lines about export controls are the outlet's. Not a new Epoch release date stated.
